body: We use a custom connector here to be able to gather every props we need before sending them to the higher component. We need to gather all those data because the external autocomplete component (here react-autosuggest) needs to be initialize with the entire state at once.
You can use `eslint-disable-line` to disable the next line.
You should bind that in the constructor so it doesn't create a new function at each `render`.
I would add more implementation details to let the user know what he/she should focus their attention on.

body: I must say, I read this part way too quickly. Being used to react-instantsearch, it's a bit confusing to have a component that will be connected and yet doesn't really have any "connection".
Maybe the fact that autocompletes in the "market" don't play nicely with instantsearch means that we have to create our own?

I made some changes about the example of an autocomplete displaying values from the same index. In this case you don't need to manage the state externally and can only use a connector.

As you can see, this connector only implement `getProvidedProps` and `refine` (to change the value of the query). In order for this to work, you still need to use `Virtual Widgets` for the search box and the facets. 

We could ship this connector with react-instantsearch but going a little bit further and adding the behavior to actually set the search parameters. What do you think?
Can't we use the source files rather than the dist?
